evals.prompt: Build a pricing card and a primary button in the Neo-Brutalism style using Tailwind v4. The project has no existing design system.
evals.expected_output: A pricing card and button that use the neo-brutalism token block through the --ui-* roles and the @theme inline mapping, with a visible focus ring and no hard-coded colours.
expectations: Uses the neo-brutalism token block via the .theme-neo-brutalism class and --ui-* roles instead of hard-coded hex values
Uses `@theme inline` (not a plain `@theme` and not a JS theme.extend) for the Tailwind v4 mapping
Includes a visible :focus-visible style and does not clip the focusable element
Handles prefers-reduced-motion for the press-offset hover effect
Does not claim a contrast ratio it did not take from the ledger or recompute

evals.prompt: Our app already has a design system with CSS variables --brand-bg, --brand-card and --brand-ink. Add a glassmorphism control bar to the dashboard header.
evals.expected_output: A glass control bar mapped onto the existing variables, without replacing the existing design system, with the glass backdrop requirements and fallbacks.
expectations: Maps the --ui-* roles onto the existing --brand-* variables (or uses them directly) and does not replace the existing design system
States or ensures the glass surface sits over a dark or saturated backdrop, and keeps the tint so white text stays legible over a light backdrop
Provides an @supports fallback for missing backdrop-filter and handles prefers-reduced-transparency
Uses a focus ring that is visible on both light and dark backdrops (two-tone or equivalent)
Does not add global .ui-card / .ui-button rules that would affect existing components

evals.prompt: I'm launching an online pharmacy. Pick a visual style for the site and explain why.
evals.expected_output: A reasoned proposal of a primary and secondary style for a healthcare-adjacent product, avoiding styles the product-fit table lists as wrong for it.
expectations: Proposes a primary and a secondary style with one reason each, using Best for and Avoid when guidance
Does not propose maximalism, cyberpunk or another style the table lists under Avoid for healthcare

Says the table has no exact online-pharmacy row and that it is working from the nearest analogue (the Healthcare or clinic row, or general e-commerce), instead of presenting its answer as an exact catalog match
Mentions at least one relevant risk or requirement from the style index (for example inputs needing the --ui-border)
Gives a recommendation with reasons and risk only, and does not write CSS or token files because the user didn't ask for them

evals.prompt: Make my site look like a Memphis-design 1980s postmodern poster with confetti shapes and zigzags.
evals.expected_output: An honest statement that no indexed style matches Memphis design, with the two closest styles clearly labelled as unverified, not presented as catalog guidance.
expectations: States that there is no verified match in the catalog for this style
Labels the two closest styles (for example maximalism and y2k or scrapbook) as unverified suggestions
If it creates a Memphis token block anyway, it labels it unverified, keeps it out of the catalog, and does not claim contrast was verified for it
If it proceeds to build anything, it takes colours from an indexed style's tokens or recomputes contrast and says so

evals.prompt: Add a Minimalism-style invoice summary card with a Pay button and a Download link to our existing dashboard page. The app already styles its own body, headings and buttons, so don't touch those. You can't open a browser here.
evals.expected_output: A scoped card (no page-level rules), controls with explicit types, contrast pairs taken from the ledger or recomputed for the surface actually used, and an honest statement that nothing was rendered.
expectations: Writes no rule whose selector is a bare html, body, * or element name, including inside media queries
Gives every button an explicit type, and uses a real link for Download
Quotes a contrast ratio only for a pair that is in the ledger on that surface, or one it recomputed, and does not reuse a ledger ratio for the same colour on a different surface
Says it did not render the result and leaves the render-only checklist items open, instead of writing rendered or checked in a browser
Shows both relative luminances beside any ratio it computes, and lists the result of searching its own files for http(s):// before it states its dependencies or fonts
Applies the same scoping rule to any demo page it builds, including the inline style block

evals.prompt: Our product page for a pair of headphones feels flat and people don't know what to tap. Rebuild the hero in the Swiss style: product name, photo, price, colour swatches and an Add to bag button. No browser is available.
evals.expected_output: A Swiss-themed hero that applies the composition moves: a decorative oversized back word behind the product photo with controls on top, the accent reserved for interactive elements, and one huge element with small supporting text, all within the contrast, focus and scoping contracts.
expectations: Reads references/composition.md and names which moves it applied and why
The oversized back word is aria-hidden and the product name also exists as real text, or its contrast is recomputed at every backdrop it crosses
The product image cannot intercept clicks (pointer-events: none or equivalent) and no control or body text is overlapped
--ui-accent appears only on interactive elements and their states, not on the price, headings, swatches' decoration or the back word
Uses one huge element with body text at least 16px and labels at least 12px, and keeps a logical heading order
Says it did not render the result and leaves the overlap, reflow and 200% zoom checks open

evals.prompt: Build me a SaaS landing page for Ledgerline, an invoicing tool for freelance illustrators. Sections: hero, how it works, pricing (Free and Studio at 12 euro a month), and a footer with Contact and Privacy. No customer names, quotes or usage numbers exist yet. No browser is available.
evals.expected_output: A landing page in an indexed style that passes the anti-slop gate (zero high tells, at most two medium tells each with a reason, graded by the frozen predicates after their exceptions), with the delivery note reporting the rubric run (version, gate result and assessed coverage, counts by id and severity, exceptions with their accepted evidence), the five Could-this-be-any-site answers with evidence, and tells kept out of any ux-laws finding.
expectations: Reads references/anti-slop.md and names the rubric version it applied (the version line at the top of that file) in the delivery note
The hero is not a centred H1, one line and two buttons: one huge element, one accent-filled action, and the second action as an outline or a text link

Graded by the frozen predicates after their exceptions: no purple-to-blue gradient, no gradient text and no hero badge, since no exception applies to this brief; blurred colour blobs or an opacity reveal on three or more sections count as medium tells unless the row's exception holds with its accepted evidence, and any medium counted stays within the gate of two with a reason

No section matches the icon-card-grid predicate (three or more equal-width cards each holding an icon, a heading and one to two lines). A parallel grid for the pricing tiers or the how-it-works steps is graded by that predicate and its exceptions, not banned
No trusted-by logo row, and no quote, star rating, statistic or customer attribution, because the brief supplied none; each one present counts as a separate unsupported attribution
The footer holds only Contact and Privacy, with no placeholder link columns
Headline and calls to action name the product and the audience (invoicing, illustrators) and use verb plus object, not Get started or Learn more alone
Answers the five Could-this-be-any-site questions, one sentence of evidence each, under their own heading in the delivery note

Reports the gate result (pass, fail or inconclusive) with assessed coverage, and tell counts per page by id and severity with zero high and at most two medium, each medium with its reason and each exception citing one of the rubric's accepted evidence types for that occurrence, and does not report any tell as a ux-laws law finding or score
Says it did not render the result and marks the render-only evidence as source only

evals.prompt: Build the home page for a wedding photographer's portfolio in the Editorial style: her name, a three-sentence bio, a featured gallery of eight photos she will supply, a short testimonial from a couple, and a Book a date link. No browser is available.
evals.expected_output: An Editorial-themed page with a two-step type scale (one huge element per view, body and meta sizes with the 16px and 12px floors), the bio in a measure of 45 to 75 characters, the editorial pairing (Playfair Display display, Newsreader body) from the token stack, section padding that varies by role using the --ui-space-* steps, the imagery kind named as photo with the treatment rules applied, an alt decision per image, nothing from the ban list, and an honest statement that nothing was rendered.
expectations: Reads references/typography.md and references/imagery.md and names the type scale and the imagery kind it chose

Applies the two-step scale, since a portfolio page is a view that takes scale contrast: display via clamp() with a vw term, body at 1rem or 1.125rem, meta between 0.8125rem and 0.875rem, no third size between the body and display steps within a view (the section display floor resolving to 32px on phones is the display step, not a violation), reading text at least 16px and labels at least 12px
Caps the bio and other reading text at a measure of 45 to 75 characters (for example max-inline-size in ch) and does not shrink text on narrow screens to fit more per line
Uses the editorial row of the pairing table (Playfair Display for display, Newsreader for body) from the existing --ui-font-display and --ui-font-body stacks, and adds no new font

Names the imagery kind as photo (the style's row), fixes every image box with aspect-ratio plus width and height, crops toward the subject, puts no tint or overlay in --ui-accent on any photo, and places the testimonial and any text over imagery on a solid panel or on a translucent panel whose text and surface pair has a worst-case ledger row

Gives every image an alt decision (a descriptive alt for the gallery photos, alt="" for decoration) and states which, and uses nothing from the ban list (no stock handshake, floating UI cards, abstract blobs or AI-generated faces presented as real people)
Because this is a page and not a component, section padding differs by section role (hero, content, band, footer) using the --ui-space-* steps, not one value for every section
Says it did not render the result and leaves the crop, reflow and 200% zoom checks open

evals.prompt: Build the hero section of a launch page for a pair of studio headphones in the Editorial style: a brand word, a two-line headline, an eyebrow, the product photo, one paragraph and a Pre-order button. The display font is self-hosted and the client wants a short loading screen before the hero animates in. Plain CSS, no animation library. No browser is available.
evals.expected_output: An Editorial hero with a loader and a choreographed reveal that follows references/choreography.md: an opaque loader that exits by transform or clip-path and gates the content, headings and decoration staggered from a --ui-stagger step with the product photo entering last, the paragraph and the button at rest from the first frame, every entrance at full opacity, a static reduced-motion end state, data-ui-motion on every moving element, and a choreography line in the delivery.
expectations: Reads references/choreography.md and delivers the order it names: the loader, then a gate that holds the content while the loader is up, then the brand word, headline lines and eyebrow one stagger step apart, and the product photo last

States the timings in a choreography line and they fit the budget: the stagger step is between 40 and 80 ms and comes from a --ui-stagger custom property, no first-screen element starts later than 600 ms, and the last element is at rest under 1.2 s
The paragraph and the Pre-order button are not animated: they are at rest from the first frame and no control or body text carries an entrance
No first-screen text fades from transparent: the headline, brand word and eyebrow enter by transform, clip-path or mask at opacity 1
Under prefers-reduced-motion the loader is not shown and every choreographed element sits at its end pose with no clip, so the page is fully readable at first paint

Every choreographed element, the loader included, carries data-ui-reveal beside data-ui-motion, and the data-ui-reveal count matches the elements the choreography line names; a hover or press effect marked data-ui-motion alone is not counted
The loader exits by transform or clip-path (not by animating its width or height), is hidden until script shows it, and the page is usable with script disabled or blocked

Saves the previous history.scrollRestoration value and restores it when the gate closes, including when the loader fails or the page is left early; skips the loader and the top scroll on reload, history (back_forward) and fragment navigation, so a reader who reloads a scrolled page keeps their position

Arms the loader's deadline when the gate is set rather than at DOMContentLoaded, ends the loader through one terminal cleanup that a late readiness callback cannot restart, and runs that cleanup when prefers-reduced-motion changes to reduce while the loader is up

The product photo has width and height (or aspect-ratio) so its box is reserved, and the loader waits for the image (decode or load) together with the display font inside the same deadline, so the subject does not finish its entrance before the image arrives; a failed or slow image never blocks the page

With the theme class on a wrapper element rather than on html, the loader shows during the gate, the entrances hold and the scroll is locked, and the loader never appears after the content has been revealed

Keyboard focus during loading cannot activate an obscured control: focus entering the covered content dismisses the loader through the same cleanup (or the covered content is inert while the gate is set)
Says it did not render the result and leaves the order, budget and reduced-motion checks open
